EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` only inserts keys into `tools_available` for the four runners it iterates. When `source_paths` is empty/nonexistent, it returns `HealthScan(elapsed_s=...)` with an empty `tools_available` map, so downstream cannot distinguish “no files scanned” from “all tools unavailable/unknown”. This crosses the insect-brain interface because the health report is supposed to provide tool availability as a structured signal every round. Simpler fix extension: always populate `tools_available` for all configured tools with explicit booleans, even on early return.

EXTEND C0021 | Timeout handling is also wrong in fix evaluation baselines and post-fix checks. `_count_tool_issues()` collapses any runner failure/timeout into `0`, so a timed-out pyright/ruff/bandit run is interpreted as “no issues”, which can make `_compute_fix_verdict()` mark a harmful or unevaluable patch as `SAFE`/`NEUTRAL`. This is higher consequence than health-scan undercounting because it drives `verified=True` propagation in the immune pipeline’s Stage 4.

FINDING_ID: F001
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports/dependencies, only the target file. In `bench/endocrine.py`, it writes just `os.path.basename(target_path)` into a tempdir, then runs pyright/ruff/bandit on that isolated file and optionally runs `test_cmd` in the tempdir. Evidence: patched file creation is `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`; no sibling modules/package tree/config files are copied, and no source root is preserved. For multi-file modules, imports now resolve against an incomplete tempdir rather than the real package layout, so tool/test outcomes are not measuring the proposed fix in a faithful sandbox.
FOLLOW: This directly affects the advertised “sandbox-test proposed fixes” feature. A fix can be falsely labeled HARMFUL because pyright/mypy/tests fail on missing local imports or absent config, even though the patch is valid in the real tree. It also permits false SAFE/NEUTRAL outcomes when tests don’t actually exercise the package because the command runs in an empty tempdir. Downstream, immune_agents.py Stage 4 uses these verdicts to set `finding.verified = True`; a bad endocrine verdict therefore changes dedup/bug-closed behavior across later rounds and can silently close or leave open the wrong bugs.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when evaluating a fix, copy the whole relevant source tree into the tempdir preserving relative paths, patch the target file in-place inside that copied tree, and run tools/tests from the copied project root instead of a single-file scratch directory.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — test execution in `evaluate_fix()` commonly runs against the wrong code. The function patches a file under `tmpdir`, but executes the caller-supplied `test_cmd` unchanged with only `cwd=tmpdir`. In context, immune_agents.py passes `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`. That path is relative to the real repo, not the tempdir, and the import path for `bench` is not rewritten to the patched sandbox. As written, tests either fail to locate `bench/tests`, or import the real package outside the sandbox rather than the patched file.
FOLLOW: This breaks the central safety claim of fix evaluation: “no source modification” plus meaningful regression testing. False failures make valid fixes look HARMFUL/UNEVALUABLE; false passes let tests validate the live repo instead of the patched copy. Because `_compute_fix_verdict()` treats `tests_passed is True` as SAFE on zero net diagnostics, this can incorrectly certify fixes. The bad verdict propagates into immune Stage 4 verification and then into NK bug-closure/escalation behavior.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — rewrite test execution to run against the copied sandbox root: copy the repository subtree needed for `bench/tests`, invoke the same command from that copied root, and ensure the patched sandbox root is first on `PYTHONPATH` for the subprocess.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can classify a fix as `SAFE` even when one tool gets worse and another improves more. Evidence: it computes `total_net = net_type_errors + net_ruff_errors + net_bandit_issues` and returns HARMFUL only if `total_net > 0`, SAFE if `total_net < 0`. A patch that introduces 3 new bandit issues but removes 5 ruff warnings yields `total_net = -2` and is marked SAFE, despite clearly regressing security. This is root-cause logic, not just threshold tuning.
FOLLOW: The verdict contract says HARMFUL means “new issues introduced”; summing nets violates that contract and silently masks regressions in one tool with improvements in another. That can wrongly mark fixes as verified in the immune pipeline, causing later duplicate suppression and closure of a bug whose accepted fix actually introduced new security/type defects. Because the PoC goal is trustworthy end-to-end firing, silently wrong SAFE judgments are HIGH severity.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — classify as HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive; classify as SAFE only when at least one net field is negative and none are positive; otherwise fall through to tests/no-change logic.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.84
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can patch the wrong file because it matches by substring containment: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path`. A basename or partial fragment mentioned in `finding.description`/`proposed_fix` can match multiple source paths, and the function returns the first hit. It then falls back to `source_paths[0]` if no match is found. Evidence: no exact disambiguation, no basename-uniqueness check, no rejection on ambiguity.
FOLLOW: Wrong-file selection makes fix evaluation untrustworthy even when patch application succeeds. The evaluator may patch an unrelated file, report UNEVALUABLE, or worse, report SAFE/HARMFUL against the wrong artifact. That pollutes `FixEvaluation.original_file`, downstream logs, and immune Stage 4 verification. Since later rounds use verified fixes for bug closure, a mistaken file target can close the wrong bug or fail to verify the right one.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require an unambiguous match: first prefer exact path matches, then unique basename matches; if multiple source paths match, return `None` and mark the fix UNEVALUABLE instead of guessing or falling back to the first source file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.80
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `scan_health()` never runs CrossHair despite endocrine.py advertising it as a tool binary and as part of the health-monitor/fix-evaluation design surface. This is distinct from dead constants alone: the operational tool loop in `scan_health()` iterates only pyright/ruff/bandit/mypy, so CrossHair can never contribute diagnostics or availability status. Evidence is the explicit runner list in `scan_health()` and the absence of any `run_crosshair()` implementation.
FOLLOW: The health scan’s structured output is incomplete relative to the module’s declared capability, so reviewers and downstream consumers get a misleading picture of “all significant features firing cleanly.” This also skews `tools_available` and tool-count metrics, and means symbolic-execution-related defects can never be surfaced by endocrine despite being part of its declared infrastructure role. For PoC this is medium-high because it is a dead feature in a core advertised capability.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — remove CrossHair from the endocrine tool surface for now: delete the unused CrossHair binary/timeout declarations and the claims that health scan includes it, until a real `run_crosshair()` path exists.
VERIFIED: TRUE
